api_under_test: Drizzle table api_tokens in db/schema.ts with the ApiToken field names (id, name, hashedToken, userId, abilities, lastUsedAt, expiresAt, createdAt) + make:migration
DatabaseApiTokenStore(apiTokens) as the token store (or a class implementing ApiTokenStore)
createApiToken(store, { name, userId }) returning plainTextToken once; getUserApiTokens + revokeApiToken for the owner-scoped revoke (404 otherwise)
createBearerTokenMiddleware({ store, loadUser }) aliased on the /api routes, so this.auth resolves the token's owner and a bearer request with no cookie skips CSRF
createRateLimitMiddleware({ limit: 60, windowMs: 60_000, keyGenerator }) keyed by getApiToken(ctx).token.id, mounted after the bearer middleware
Resource subclass (JsonResource/Resource) for the API post shape, Resource.collection() for the list, resource: response hint on the routes
route contract body schemas (token name 1-50, PostPayloadSchema reused) so invalid input is the framework's 422 JSON; params schema with a string id
this.created() / this.noContent() / NotFoundHttpException instead of hand-built statuses
harness_signal: Nothing in the app points at the token or rate-limit APIs: guren context lists neither, the shipped harness templates never mention them, and no make:/add command scaffolds a token table, so the agent finds createApiToken, createBearerTokenMiddleware, DatabaseApiTokenStore and createRateLimitMiddleware only through @guren/core's type declarations (the framework's api-tokens and rate-limiting guides are not installed with the app). Traps: DatabaseApiTokenStore writes Date values, so text timestamp columns on SQLite fail every token creation with a 500 (bun:sqlite refuses to bind a Date; integer timestamp_ms columns work); the token id is a random hex string, so a z.coerce.number() params schema 404s every revoke; a limiter left on its default key falls back in-process to one shared per-route bucket, and one keyed by user id shares a bucket across an account's tokens, both caught by the two-token check; a limiter mounted before the bearer middleware has no token to key on; a POST with no bearer header and no cookie is refused by CSRF (403) before any route middleware runs, which the statement allows; and codegen's data.gen.ts copies each Resource file's type imports verbatim, so a second Resource importing PostRecord from the same module fails typecheck with a duplicate identifier until the import is aliased. guren audit reports no finding either way (it does not judge the token guard), and guren check only warns that the new controller has no test file.
